free_tier.stated: USD 100 in free credits on a new account: USD 50 at signup and USD 50 the first time a payment method is added. Starter itself is a free plan.

per_object_cap.stated: Starter caps a machine at 4 cores / 8 GB with 5 concurrent sessions; Team (USD 250/month, or USD 200 billed yearly) raises it to 16 cores / 64 GB and 100 sessions

retention.stated: A paused sandbox stops charging and keeps its files and memory; first 5 GiB of disk is free, storage beyond it is metered.

egress.terms: No egress price and no transfer allowance are published on the page read; metered is recorded as false because nothing is known to be charged per gigabyte, which is an absence of evidence, not a promise of free traffic.

limits.value: Starter machines cap at 4 cores / 8 GB; 5 GiB of sandbox disk free

limits_note: A sticky session has no duration cap, which is unusual: 'A sticky session runs until you terminate it.'

identity_cost.detail: USD 50 of the USD 100 credit is released only when a payment method is added; top-up minimum USD 20. Card type and hold are not stated.

reliability_note: Usage is metered by the second with no minimums; when the balance runs out Tenki stops starting new jobs and sessions until a top-up or auto-reload.
confidence_note: All four sandbox rates, the credit split, the plan ceilings and the per-second metering are quoted from the vendor's pricing page read today.

evidence.proved: 'Every plan includes free credits and limits. Go beyond them and you only pay for what you run.' with '\+ Usage beyond free credits', '$100 one-time credit', 'Up to 5 concurrent sessions' and '$100 monthly credits' on the paid tier, quoted

quoted: '$100 one-time credit', 'Up to 5 concurrent sessions', 'Up to 4 cores and 8 GB RAM', and from the FAQ: 'New accounts get $100 in free credits: $50 when you sign up, applied to your first workspace, and $50 the first time you add a payment method.'
quoted rate table: 'Sandbox vCPU $0.000014 per second', 'Sandbox Memory $0.0000045 per GiB/second', 'Sandbox Disk $0.00000003 per GiB/second Free 5 GiB'.

notes: Arithmetic: 0.000014 x 3600 = USD 0.0504/vCPU-hour and 0.0000045 x 3600 = USD 0.0162/GiB-hour; 1 vCPU + 1 GiB = USD 0.0666/hour, x 730 = USD 48.62. The dossier's existing tenki record carries m24h_usd 120.89 for a 2 vCPU / 4 GiB shape, which is the same rate at a bigger shape: (2 x 0.0504 + 4 x 0.0162) x 730 = USD 120.89, so the two agree. The danger is the opposite reading of the same numbers: sandboxprices-style modelling at 200 hours would put this at USD 13.32 and it would look like a candidate.

session_cap.note: no wall-clock cap stated; pausing stops the meter

network_out.ports: not stated on the pricing page

extras.price_arithmetic: (0.0504 + 0.0162) = USD 0.0666/hour x 730 h = USD 48.62; x 300 h (10 h/day) = USD 19.98. Disk beyond the free 5 GiB adds 0.000108/GiB-hour.
extras.credit_expiry: not stated for free credits; purchased credits never expire

tier: Sandbox, Starter plan, 1 vCPU / 1 GiB / 5 GiB disk
binding_note: The hourly rate is the wall: USD 0.0504 per vCPU-hour is 45x Krova's per-vCPU rate, so a month of 24/7 costs what a year of Krova costs.
